title: India Sweeps Three Weightlifting Medals on Golden Day at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
excerpt: Mirabai Chanu clinches record-breaking third consecutive gold while Rishikanta Singh and Muthupandi Raja add silver medals.
body:
• Mirabai Chanu won her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold in the women's 48kg with a Games-record total of 190kg
  • Rishikanta Singh Chanambam claimed silver in the men's 60kg behind Malaysia's Aniq Kasdan, who set a Games record of 273kg
  • Muthupandi Raja secured silver in the men's 65kg with 286kg as Malaysia's Aznil Bidin took gold at a Games-record 299kg
  • India's three-medal haul in a single day marks the country's strongest weightlifting showing at any Commonwealth Games in recent memory

India delivered a commanding performance on the weightlifting platform at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Saturday, collecting one gold and two silver medals across three events to cement its position as the sport's dominant force at this edition of the Games.

Mirabai Makes History With Third Straight Gold

Mirabai Chanu cemented her status as one of India's greatest athletes with a commanding victory in the women's 48kg category. The Manipuri lifter, who won Olympic silver in Tokyo, overcame a shaky start — missing her opening snatch attempt at 82kg — before roaring back with a Commonwealth Games record of 85kg on her final snatch lift.

She missed her first clean and jerk attempt at 105kg but kept her composure and nailed it on the second try, finishing with a combined total of 190kg that set a new Games record. Nigeria's Ruth Asuquo Nyong took silver with 168kg while Malaysia's Irene Jane Henry claimed bronze at 167kg.

"I was confident she would win. She has worked so hard for this."

— Mirabai Chanu's mother, speaking after the gold medal performance

Mirabai won silver on her debut in Glasgow back in 2014 before claiming back-to-back golds at Gold Coast 2018 and Birmingham 2022. Her coach Vijay Sharma has guided her through a remarkable run that includes multiple national records set earlier this year — 89kg in snatch, 116kg in clean and jerk, and a 205kg total at the National Championships.

Rishikanta and Raja Add Silver Medals

Earlier in the day, Rishikanta Singh Chanambam delivered a solid performance in the men's 60kg final, lifting a total of 264kg to claim silver. Malaysia's Aniq Kasdan dominated the category with a Games-record total of 273kg, while Kenya's Joshua Amunga Mboya finished with bronze at 260kg.

In the evening session, Muthupandi Raja competed in the men's 65kg final and secured silver with a total of 286kg — 126kg in the snatch and 160kg in clean and jerk. Raja had a technically difficult outing, missing his opening snatch attempt before successfully lifting 126kg on his second try. Malaysia's Aznil Bidin was in imperious form, setting a Games record of 299kg to take gold. Papua New Guinea's Morea Baru rounded out the podium with bronze at 282kg.

What's Next for India's Lifters

India's weightlifting campaign continues with Ajaya Babu Valluri in the men's 79kg category, where he enters as a favourite after winning the 2025 Commonwealth Championships. Gyaneshwari Yadav and Bindyarani Devi will compete in the women's 53kg and 58kg events respectively, both ranked second among Commonwealth lifters.

The three-medal haul in Glasgow sends a clear signal: India's weightlifting programme, anchored by Mirabai's excellence and supported by a rising generation of talent, remains the country's most reliable medal factory at the Commonwealth Games.
